practiceQuestions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution of India is the office of the Attorney-General of India provided?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 76 of the Indian Constitution provides for the office of the Attorney-General of India, who is the highest law officer in the country. Article 165 relates to the Advocate-General of a State.

practiceQuestions.q: Who has the authority to appoint the Attorney-General of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Attorney-General of India is appointed by the President on the advice of the Union Cabinet (headed by the Prime Minister).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the prescribed tenure of the Attorney-General of India under the Constitution?
opts: 6 years or up to 65 years of age
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constitution does not fix the term of the Attorney-General. He holds office during the pleasure of the President.

practiceQuestions.q: To be appointed as the Attorney-General of India, a person must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of which court?
practiceQuestions.sol: A person to be appointed Attorney-General must be qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court (i.e., judge of a HC for 5 years or advocate of a HC for 10 years or an eminent jurist).

practiceQuestions.q: Can the Attorney-General of India participate in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament?
opts: Yes, but only in the Lok Sabha
Yes, in either House or any joint sitting
Yes, only when a constitutional amendment is discussed
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 88, the Attorney-General has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of either House, joint sittings, and any committee of Parliament of which he may be named a member.

practiceQuestions.q: Does the Attorney-General of India have the right to vote in Parliament?
opts: Yes, only in case of a tie
No, he does not have the right to vote
practiceQuestions.sol: Although the Attorney-General can speak and participate in parliamentary proceedings, Article 88 explicitly states that he does NOT have the right to vote.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the Attorney-General submit his resignation when he wishes to step down?
practiceQuestions.sol: Since the Attorney-General is appointed by the President and holds office during his pleasure, he submits his resignation to the President.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is true regarding the remuneration of the Attorney-General of India?
opts: It is fixed by the Constitution.
It is determined by the Parliament.
It is determined by the President.
He receives no remuneration as it is an honorary post.
practiceQuestions.sol: The remuneration of the Attorney-General is not specified in the Constitution; it is determined by the President.

practiceQuestions.q: Assisting the Attorney-General in his official duties are the Solicitor General of India and:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Attorney-General is assisted by the Solicitor-General of India and several Additional Solicitors-General to fulfill legal duties.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following expressions best describes the nature of the Attorney-General's office?
opts: A member of the Union Cabinet
Not a full-time counsel and not a government servant
A judicial officer of the Supreme Court
practiceQuestions.sol: The Attorney-General is not a full-time counsel for the Government and does not fall in the category of government servants; hence, he is not debarred from private legal practice.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Attorney-General not considered a debarred political appointee in terms of private practice, unlike standard government officials?
opts: Because he is an elected representative of the public.
Because his office is non-political and he is not a member of the cabinet, though appointed on political advice.
Because the Supreme Court explicitly ordered private practice rights.
Because he receives a nominal salary which forces him to take private briefs.
practiceQuestions.sol: The AG is not a full-time government employee. He is a primary legal advisor, but since he is not a member of the Cabinet, he is permitted to practice privately, subject to certain professional restrictions (e.g., not advising against the Government).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary constitutional rationale behind granting the Attorney-General the right to audience in all courts within the territory of India?
opts: To enable him to supervise lower judiciary appointments.
To ensure that the Union Government's legal interests and viewpoints are effectively represented everywhere.
To give him precedence over the Chief Justice of India.
To allow him to inspect prison conditions across states.
practiceQuestions.sol: The right of audience in all courts gives the AG the unrestricted legal locus standi to represent the Government of India in any judicial forum across the nation.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the convention regarding the resignation of the Attorney-General operate when a change occurs in the Union Government (Council of Ministers)?
opts: He automatically continues for his statutory 5-year term unaffected.
Conventionally, he resigns when the government resigns or is replaced, requiring the new government to make a fresh appointment.
He must be impeached by a joint session of Parliament.
He becomes the head of the caretaker government.
practiceQuestions.sol: Since the AG is appointed on the advice of the cabinet, convention dictates that when the government resigns, the AG also resigns, and the new government appoints its choice.

practiceQuestions.q: Which restriction is explicitly placed on the private practice of the Attorney-General?
opts: He cannot appear in any criminal matter anywhere.
He cannot advise or hold a brief against the Government of India or defend accused persons in criminal cases without government permission.
He cannot take up cases involving private corporate entities.
He cannot charge any fee for private consultancy.
practiceQuestions.sol: To avoid conflict of interest, the AG must not advise against the Government of India, defend accused persons in criminal prosecutions without government clearance, or accept appointment as a director in any company without permission.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the relationship between the Attorney-General and parliamentary committees?
opts: He can vote in any parliamentary committee he joins.
He has the right to speak and take part in any committee of Parliament of which he is named a member, but without voting rights.
He acts as the permanent chairman of all parliamentary joint committees.
He is prohibited from entering any parliamentary committee room.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 88 extends his rights to committees of Parliament of which he is named a member, giving him the right to speak and participate, though still lacking the right to vote.

practiceQuestions.q: In terms of legal hierarchy and precedence of state dignitaries, where does the Attorney-General stand approximately?
opts: He is not included in the official Table of Precedence.
He is positioned at a specific rank in the Table of Precedence, typically below Union Cabinet Ministers.
Above the Chief Justice of India
practiceQuestions.sol: The Attorney-General occupies a well-defined place in the Government of India's Table of Precedence (usually placed around rank 11A, below Cabinet Ministers).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following describes a key difference between the Attorney-General of India and the Advocate-General of a State?
opts: AG is appointed under Article 76 by the President, whereas Advocate-General is appointed under Article 165 by the Governor.
AG has voting rights in Parliament, while Advocate-General does not have voting rights in the State Legislature.
AG can be removed only by impeachment, whereas Advocate-General serves at pleasure.
AG is a full-time government servant, whereas Advocate-General is not.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 76 governs the AG (appointed by President), while Article 165 governs the Advocate-General of a State (appointed by the Governor). Both lack voting rights in their respective legislatures.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the Attorney-General be called upon to give legal advice on matters referred to him by the President?
opts: No, he only advises the Supreme Court.
Yes, giving advice on legal matters referred by the President is a core constitutional duty under Article 76(2).
Only if the Lok Sabha passes a resolution.
No, he only represents the executive in court and cannot give advisory opinions.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 76(2) explicitly states that it is the duty of the Attorney-General to give advice to the Government of India upon such legal matters, and to perform such other duties of a legal character, as may from time to time be referred or assigned by the President.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the status of the Attorney-General regarding parliamentary privileges and immunities under Article 105?
opts: He enjoys all the privileges and immunities available to a Member of Parliament.
He has no parliamentary immunities since he is not elected.
He enjoys immunity only from criminal arrest, not from civil suits.
He enjoys privileges only when the Prime Minister is present.
practiceQuestions.sol: By virtue of his right to speak and participate in parliamentary proceedings under Article 88, he also enjoys the privileges and immunities of an MP as specified in Article 105.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Constitution not prescribe specific qualifications for the removal of the Attorney-General?
opts: Because he is appointed for a permanent lifetime tenure.
Because he holds office during the pleasure of the President, aligning with the executive's confidence.
Because the Supreme Court handles his removal directly.
Because he can only be removed by a unanimous vote of all state legislatures.
practiceQuestions.sol: The 'pleasure of the President' doctrine means the executive can terminate his appointment at any time without needing to prove any misconduct or pass a parliamentary resolution.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Attorney-General of India:
1. He is the first law officer of the Government of India.
2. He must be a member of either House of Parliament at the time of his appointment.
3. He has the right of audience in all courts within the territory of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: AG is the highest law officer. Statement 2 is incorrect: He is not required to be a member of Parliament, though he can participate in parliamentary proceedings. Statement 3 is correct: He has the right of audience in all courts across India.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the constitutional provisions governing the Attorney-General:
1. The Constitution has fixed the term of office of the Attorney-General to 5 years.
2. The remuneration of the Attorney-General is charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and determined by Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is wrong because the Constitution does not fix his term. Statement 2 is wrong because his remuneration is not determined by Parliament; rather, it is determined by the President (and it is not explicitly mentioned as charged expenditure in the Constitution like that of CAG or SC judges).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the duties of the Attorney-General:
1. To give advice to the Government of India upon legal matters referred by the President.
2. To perform other duties of a legal character assigned to him by the President.
3. To discharge the functions conferred on him by the Constitution or any other law.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements accurately reflect the duties assigned to the Attorney-General under Article 76(2) and other statutes (such as representing the government in certain tribunals or Supreme Court cases).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the rights of the Attorney-General in Parliament:
1. He can participate in the deliberations of both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
2. He has the right to vote in case of a tie in parliamentary committees of which he is a member.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: He can speak and participate in proceedings of both Houses under Article 88. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 88 explicitly denies him the right to vote under any circumstances, including ties in committees.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the limitations on the Attorney-General:
1. He is barred from accepting private legal practice or taking up any brief against the Union Government under any circumstances.
2. He cannot be appointed as a director in any company without the permission of the Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because he is NOT completely barred from private legal practice; he can take private briefs as long as they do not conflict with government interests or involve defending accused persons in criminal prosecutions without clearance. Statement 2 is correct: He cannot accept a directorship in a company without government permission.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Solicitor-General of India:
1. The office of the Solicitor-General is explicitly created and defined under Article 76 of the Constitution.
2. The Solicitor-General assists the Attorney-General in fulfilling his official legal responsibilities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 76 mentions only the Attorney-General; it does not mention the Solicitor-General or Additional Solicitors-General (they are statutory/executive-created offices to assist the AG). Statement 2 is correct: They assist the AG.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the Attorney-General of India and the Advocate-General of a State:
1. Both hold office during the pleasure of the President.
2. Both are entitled to speak and take part in the proceedings of the respective legislatures without the right to vote.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Advocate-General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor, not the President. Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 88 and Article 177 respectively, both have the right to speak in their respective legislatures without voting rights.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the legal representation of the Union Government:
1. The Attorney-General represents the Government of India in all cases in the Supreme Court in which the Government of India is concerned.
2. He also appears on behalf of the Government of India in any High Court in any case in which the Government of India is concerned.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: One of the primary duties is to appear on behalf of GoI in the Supreme Court. Statement 2 is incorrect as a sweeping rule: While he *can* appear in any High Court, the rule states he represents GoI in the Supreme Court and references to High Courts typically occur when instructed or when required, but duties specifically mandate Supreme Court appearance. The standard text states: (a) to give advice... (b) to appear in Supreme Court on behalf of GoI; (c) to represent GoI in any High Court reference under Article 143.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the disqualifications and background required for the Attorney-General:
1. A person must have been a judge of a High Court for 5 years or an advocate of a High Court for 10 years to be appointed.
2. An eminent jurist can also be appointed as the Attorney-General of India by the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The qualifications for the Attorney-General are the same as those required for a judge of the Supreme Court, which include: (a) judge of a High Court for 5 years, or (b) advocate of a High Court for 10 years, or (c) an eminent jurist in the opinion of the President.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal and resignation of the Attorney-General:
1. The procedure for the removal of the Attorney-General is explicitly laid down in the Constitution, requiring a two-thirds majority in Parliament.
2. The Attorney-General may resign his office by writing under his hand addressed to the Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is wrong because the Constitution does not lay down any impeachment or removal procedure; he holds office during the pleasure of the President. Statement 2 is wrong because he submits his resignation to the President, not the Prime Minister.
